rv.q: The Bitter Earth is a play of extraordinary power, performed and staged with creativity, talent and expertise.
Thanks to great work by Lolar-Johnson, Godwaldt, and Rhoze, This Bitter Earth, the play, is as emotionally evocative as “This Bitter Earth,” the song.

Matthew Lolar-Johnson, meanwhile, invests Jesse with such understated realness that, by the show's bittersweet conclusion, the character should seem as real as the audience members tearfully breathing next to you.

This intimate portrait has to do with how these two men from very different circumstances internalize well-publicized incidents involving police brutality and the killings of several African Americans that have led to the eruption of major public protests in U.S. cities.

cn.t: Critics praise Harrison David Rivers's powerful two-character drama for its beautifully articulated exploration of race, activism, and love through an interracial gay couple navigating police brutality and Black Lives Matter.
